supervisor_text: \textbf{Outlook.} A natural next step is evaluation on openly available empirical contact networks, for example the SocioPatterns high-school contact data \cite{mastrandrea2015} and primary-school contact data \cite{stehle2011,gemmetto2014}. Their class labels provide community partitions, and measured contacts permit comparison of a full-network reference with an interface retaining only $W_{ij}$. A first study could use explicitly defined static contact aggregates; retaining the recorded contact times would require a temporal-network extension. Proper evaluation must address observation windows, contact-weight calibration, incomplete participation, and sensitivity to disease parameters and community definitions. These tasks warrant a dedicated follow-up paper beyond the present methodological study. Such data test fidelity on observed contact structures; validation against observed epidemic outcomes would require additional evidence.

added_sentences: Geographically explicit synthetic networks provide another setting for evaluation \cite{jiang2024synthetic}.
Residential locations can define city or regional communities, with individual connections retained for the full-network reference and aggregated into $W_{ij}$ for the two-scale model.

Where individual connections between communities are unavailable, local contact networks can be constructed from demographic data and linked using weights informed by commuting flows \cite{tulchinsky2024networks,tizzoni2014mobility}.
This requires an explicit assumption about how mobility translates into contact intensity.
